meta.title: Stationhead, {{spanPhrase}}
meta.description: What happened on Stationhead in {{spanPhrase}}. Artists and fans listening to the same song at the same time. Every show can be played back.

og.description: 115,672 streams in under two hours, run by the artist's own account. 110 of 1,052 listeners bought the record during the show. {{CountCap}} {{show}}, all of them replayable.
og.twitterDescription: 115,672 streams in under two hours. 110 of 1,052 listeners bought the record during the show.

intro.h1: Stationhead is the home of social listening.
intro.lead: Artists and fans listening to the same song at the same time. Every play runs through the listener's own paid account, so every play is a real stream.
body: {{CountCap}} {{show}} from {{spanPhrase}}. Every one of them can be played back.
BTS ran the listening party for NORMAL from their own account. Forty two songs, and every play came off a fan's own paid subscription.

events.herolbl: streams from 7,546 people, on eight songs
body: Eight songs, forty seven minutes, and each person played them twelve times over. The group hosted it.

events.herolbl: listeners on release day, the biggest show in two months
body: Three shows ran for the release. The chat moved between Thai, Indonesian and English for nearly four hours.
The group announced it, played thirteen songs, and were off in under an hour.

events.herolbl: listeners bought the record during the show
body: Online retail converts in low single digits. This show converted at ten percent, with no campaign running behind it.

events.herolbl: on the mic, and the show ran for hours around it
body: She spoke for three and a half minutes, then stayed in the chat. That was the whole ask, and the show carried on for hours.

events.herolbl: messages a minute, three years after release
body: A Tuesday night, for an album three years old. Catalogue still pulls a full show here.

events.herolbl: on a tenth anniversary, hosted by the group
body: Ten years of catalogue, played end to end by the group themselves.
An album's first birthday. Nearly ten thousand people came back for a record they already owned.

events.herolbl: came for a show the label hosted itself
body: Label staff and a guest, on air for two hours. Five thousand people stayed for it.

events.herolbl: streams in six days, with nothing promoted
body: Five shows in six days, opened by fans, with no release to push. This is the baseline an artist walks into.

events.herolbl: plays in a day, with the group hosting
body: Four nights running, on the mic every night. The channel ran at 1.7 times its usual while they were on.

pattern.h2: The audience runs daily. The artist makes it spike.
body: Fans keep it warm every day. You bring the spike: across the shows we have measured, the day the artist joined ran between two and forty times an ordinary day on that channel.
Use it where you already have a moment. A release, an anniversary, a tour announce.

archive.intro: Older shows. The numbers are as they were reported at the time.
archive.emptyNote: Nothing has rolled off the last three weeks yet.

static.h2: It takes a date and an artist handle.
ol: Confirm the channel. If fans built one already, we connect it rather than starting again.
Pick a time that suits the fans, not the office, and tell the regular hosts first. They fill the show before you post anything.
Announce it from the artist account. Date, time, time zone, one link.
Go live from a phone. Connect the streaming account, queue a few songs, say hello.
On air, read names out, take requests, and say the channel stays open when you go.
static.note: One week is comfortable. Two days is possible.

static.h2: Four things, all of them quick.
ul: Digital purchase. The single or album, bought during the show. About a week.
Shopify shop. Your existing store, opened inside the show. About a week.
Voice note. Thirty seconds recorded on a phone, for when a live date will not work. Two days.
Fan Channel. The permanent home fans join once and keep between releases. A few days.
static.note: To start we need the artist handle, a date, and anything you want to sell. We will build the show around it.
